title: Pinching a Free Normal Cover: Variable Critical Exponent in a Quasiconformal Teichmuller Space
oneLine: A fixed free normal cover is argued to give infinitely many all-Fuchsian critical exponents approaching one from below, with an explicit linear pinching rate and a carefully limited relation to AIM Problem 4.3.
abstract: This anonymous, AI-assisted, unrefereed candidate studies AIM-TOPOLOGY-0203. For every genus g at least 2, it fixes the kernel of a surface-group epimorphism onto the nonamenable free group F_g. Across marked compact hyperbolic metrics, the resulting infinitely generated first-kind Fuchsian groups lie in one reduced surface-based quasiconformal Teichmuller space and in the all-Fuchsian locus of the corresponding AIM group-deformation space. Nonamenability forces every exponent below one. Simultaneously pinching a complete cut system to length ell gives a fixed-width Rayleigh test and the rate 1-delta=O_g(ell), so the exponent approaches one and assumes infinitely many values. Astala and Zinsmeister (1995) appear already to answer the existential question under a broader quasi-Fuchsian group-deformation reading; this release is framed as an all-Fuchsian strengthening and as a direct solution candidate only under the reduced surface-based reading. Producer replay and internal role-separated review reached PASS_WITH_NOTES. No historical-priority, unaffiliated-reproduction, formal-verification, specialist-review or peer-review claim is made.
narration: Can an infinitely generated Fuchsian group change its critical exponent without leaving one quasiconformal deformation space? This anonymous, unrefereed candidate gives an all-Fuchsian construction. Start with a closed surface of genus at least two and map its fundamental group onto a nonabelian free group by killing a complete cut system. The fixed kernel defines a regular normal cover. For every marked compact hyperbolic metric, its Fuchsian image is infinitely generated and of the first kind. Because the deck group is nonamenable, a theorem of Dougall and Sharp forces the critical exponent below one. Now pinch every cut curve to the same small length. A function supported on one lifted cell changes only across fixed-width pieces of the long collars, so its spectral energy is proportional to the pinching length while its mass stays bounded below. Sullivan's spectrum-exponent formula then makes the critical exponent approach one from below, at a linear one-sided rate. Therefore it takes infinitely many distinct values. The scope is important. Astala and Zinsmeister appear already to provide an affirmative precedent under a broad quasi-Fuchsian reading of the AIM problem. This candidate stays entirely in the Fuchsian locus and is a direct AIM solution candidate only under the reduced surface-based reading. Producer replay and internal editorial checks are not independent reconstruction, external specialist review, formal verification, peer review, novelty or priority evidence. The synthetic-voice briefing is a communication aid, not additional mathematical evidence.

problem.name: AIM Problem 4.3: variation of critical exponent in reduced quasiconformal Teichmuller space

keyResults: For every genus g at least 2, one fixed kernel of a surface-group epimorphism onto F_g is argued to give infinitely generated first-kind Fuchsian groups across all marked compact-base metrics.
The marked covers lie in one reduced surface-based quasiconformal Teichmuller space and, by reflected sphere extensions, in the all-Fuchsian locus of the AIM group-deformation space.
Nonamenability of F_g forces the critical exponent strictly below one for every marked compact-base metric.
Along simultaneous cut-system pinching to length ell, a fixed-width collar test gives 1-delta=O_g(ell) and delta approaches one from below, hence infinitely many exponent values.

Under a broad group-deformation reading, Astala-Zinsmeister (1995) appears already affirmative; the present contribution is an all-Fuchsian strengthening and a direct AIM solution candidate only under the reduced surface-based reading.
